title: Tony's Pizza hits the road: commercial auto
summary: Ride along with Tony's Pizza vans in Detroit: Business Auto symbols, physical damage, garagekeepers, endorsements and federal truck limits.
objectives: Read the Business Auto symbols, including hired vs non-owned and symbol 7's 30-day rule
Tell Specified Causes of Loss, Comprehensive and Collision apart
Spot the liability extras and exclusions, and tell an auto from mobile equipment
Pick a garagekeepers basis, and know key endorsements, forms and federal truck minimums

scenes.title: Tony's Pizza hits the road
scenes.subtitle: Symbols, physical damage, garagekeepers and endorsements (2020 ISO Business Auto, CA 00 01 11 20)

beats.text: Detroit. Tony's Pizza delivers in a brand-new van, and Dana writes its coverage on the 2020 Business Auto form.
beats.say: Detroit. Tony's Pizza delivers in a brand-new van, and Dana writes its coverage on the twenty twenty Business Auto form.

beats.text: Hot pizza, fast wheels. What could go wrong?
beats.say: Hot pizza, fast wheels. What could go wrong?

draw.text: 5 sections: covered autos, liability, physical damage, conditions, definitions
Garage form and Business Auto Physical Damage form
Motor Carrier: for-hire and private carriers

beats.text: Tony's van goes on the Business Auto form. Its five sections: covered autos, liability, physical damage, conditions and definitions.
beats.say: Tony's van goes on the Business Auto form. Its five sections: covered autos, liability, physical damage, conditions and definitions.

beats.text: The Garage form combined liability, garagekeepers and physical damage. The Business Auto Physical Damage form gave physical damage only. Both were eliminated in 2013.
beats.say: The Garage form combined liability, garagekeepers and physical damage. The Business Auto Physical Damage form gave physical damage only. Both were eliminated in twenty thirteen.

beats.text: The Truckers form was written for hauling property by auto for hire. The broader Motor Carrier form also fits private carriers hauling their own goods.
beats.say: The Truckers form was written for hauling property by auto for hire. The broader Motor Carrier form also fits private carriers hauling their own goods.

scenes.title: Covered auto symbols
scenes.src: CA 00 01 11 20, Sec. I.A-B; adapted from memory hook mn_auto-24
scenes.plain: A number next to each coverage on the declarations. It tells you which autos get that coverage.
scenes.example: Tony's own van: owned, so symbol 2 fits. A car he rents for a weekend: hired, symbol 8. Any auto at all: symbol 1.
scenes.exam: 1 any auto. 2 to 6 owned. 7 specifically described. 8 hired, not from employees. 9 non-owned. 19 mobile equipment under compulsory or FR laws.

beats.text: Symbols: numbers on the declarations that say which autos get each coverage. Symbol 1 means any auto.
beats.say: Symbols: numbers on the declarations that say which autos get each coverage. Symbol one means any auto.

beats.text: 2 through 6 are owned autos: 2 all owned, 3 private passenger, 4 other than private passenger. 5 is subject to no-fault, 6 to a compulsory uninsured motorists law.
beats.say: Two through six are owned autos: two all owned, three private passenger, four other than private passenger. Five is subject to no-fault, six to a compulsory uninsured motorists law.

beats.text: 7 is specifically described autos. 8 is hired, 9 is non-owned, and 19 is mobile equipment subject to a compulsory or financial responsibility law.
beats.say: Seven is specifically described autos. Eight is hired, nine is non-owned, and nineteen is mobile equipment subject to a compulsory or financial responsibility law.

beats.text: Watch out: only symbol 7 makes you tell the insurer about a newly acquired auto within 30 days.
beats.say: Watch out: only symbol seven makes you tell the insurer about a newly acquired auto within thirty days.

scenes.title: Tony's call: the drivers' own cars
scenes.src: CA 00 01 11 20, Sec. I.A (symbols 2, 8, 9), Sec. IV.B.5; question auto-061; memory hook mn_auto-24

beats.text: My drivers deliver in their own cars now. Am I covered if one crashes?
beats.say: My drivers deliver in their own cars now. Am I covered if one crashes?

beats.text: His liability shows only symbol 2. What should he do?
beats.say: His liability shows only symbol two. What should he do?

options.label: Nothing. Symbol 2 already covers those cars
options.fail: Symbol 2 means owned autos only. Tony doesn't own his drivers' cars.

beats.text: A driver crashes on a delivery. Symbol 2 is owned autos only, so that car isn't a covered auto for Tony's liability.
beats.say: A driver crashes on a delivery. Symbol two is owned autos only, so that car isn't a covered auto for Tony's liability.

options.label: Add symbol 9, non-owned autos
options.win: Symbol 9 covers autos Tony doesn't own, lease, hire, rent or borrow, including employees' cars used in his business.

beats.text: Covered for liability. Symbol 9 makes employees' cars covered autos while used in Tony's business.
beats.say: Covered for liability. Symbol nine makes employees' cars covered autos while used in Tony's business.

options.label: Add symbol 8, hired autos
options.fail: Symbol 8 covers autos Tony leases, hires, rents or borrows, but not ones borrowed from his own employees.

beats.text: Nope. Hired autos leave out cars borrowed from your own employees.
beats.say: Nope. Hired autos leave out cars borrowed from your own employees.

reveal.text: Hired is 8, non-owned is 9. For autos he owns, Tony's policy is primary and pays first. For others, it's excess over other insurance.
reveal.say: Hired is eight, non-owned is nine. For autos he owns, Tony's policy is primary and pays first. For others, it's excess over other insurance.

scenes.title: Tony's call: van number two
scenes.src: CA 00 01 11 20, Sec. I.B; question auto-060; memory hook mn_auto-24

beats.text: For physical damage, Tony's one van is described on the declarations: symbol 7. In March, he buys a second.
beats.say: For physical damage, Tony's one van is described on the declarations: symbol seven. In March, he buys a second.

beats.text: Van number two! Is it covered already?
beats.say: Van number two! Is it covered already?

options.label: Nothing. New vans are covered automatically
options.fail: Only symbols 1 to 6 and 19 cover new autos automatically. Under symbol 7, you must tell the insurer within 30 days.

beats.text: Day 45 after buying it, hail dents the new van. Tony never told the insurer, so it isn't a covered auto for physical damage.
beats.say: Day forty-five after buying it, hail dents the new van. Tony never told the insurer, so it isn't a covered auto for physical damage.

options.label: Have Dana tell the insurer within 30 days
options.win: Under symbol 7, a new auto is covered if all owned autos already have that coverage, or it's a replacement, and you tell the insurer within 30 days.

beats.text: Smart. Every auto he owned already had that coverage, and Dana tells the insurer within 30 days. Covered.
beats.say: Smart. Every auto he owned already had that coverage, and Dana tells the insurer within thirty days. Covered.

reveal.text: Symbols 1 to 6 and 19 cover new autos automatically. Under symbol 7, tell the insurer within 30 days.
reveal.say: Symbols one to six and nineteen cover new autos automatically. Under symbol seven, tell the insurer within thirty days.

scenes.title: Damage to the van itself
scenes.plain: Physical damage coverage for a short, named list of causes. Not on the list? Not covered.
scenes.example: Tony chose only Specified Causes for his van. A flood soaks the parked van: covered. The van hits a deer: not on the list, so not covered.
scenes.exam: Glass breakage, hitting a bird or animal, falling objects or missiles: Comprehensive. Hitting an object: Collision.

beats.text: Now the van itself: three physical damage coverages. Comprehensive, Specified Causes of Loss, and Collision.
beats.say: Now the van itself: three physical damage coverages. Comprehensive, Specified Causes of Loss, and Collision.

beats.text: Its list: fire, lightning, explosion, theft. Windstorm, hail, earthquake, flood. Vandalism. And the sinking, burning, collision or derailment of a conveyance carrying the van, like a ferry.
beats.say: Its list: fire, lightning, explosion, theft. Windstorm, hail, earthquake, flood. Vandalism. And the sinking, burning, collision or derailment of a conveyance carrying the van, like a ferry.

beats.text: Tony chose only Specified Causes: a flood is covered, a deer isn't.
beats.say: Tony chose only Specified Causes: a flood is covered, a deer isn't.

beats.text: Glass breakage, hitting a bird or animal, and falling objects are paid under Comprehensive. The van hitting an object is Collision.
beats.say: Glass breakage, hitting a bird or animal, and falling objects are paid under Comprehensive. The van hitting an object is Collision.

scenes.title: Only Specified Causes: covered?
scenes.src: CA 00 01 11 20, Sec. III.A.1 and A.3; questions auto-gap-16, auto-gap-20

cards.text: A flood soaks Tony's van while it's parked.
cards.why: Flood is on the Specified Causes list.

cards.text: The van hits a deer on a country road at dusk.
cards.why: Hitting a bird or animal is paid under Comprehensive. It isn't on the Specified Causes list.

cards.text: A rock thrown up by a passing truck cracks the windshield.
cards.why: Glass breakage is paid under Comprehensive, not Specified Causes.
Mischief or vandalism is on the Specified Causes list.

cards.text: The van slides into a guardrail on an icy ramp.
cards.why: Hitting an object is Collision coverage, not a specified cause.

cards.text: Hail dents the van's roof in a summer storm.
cards.why: Windstorm, hail or earthquake is on the Specified Causes list.

beats.text: Your turn. Tony's vans have only Specified Causes. Covered or not?
beats.say: Your turn. Tony's vans have only Specified Causes. Covered or not?

reveal.text: Flood, vandalism and hail are on the list. Deer and glass: Comprehensive. The guardrail: Collision.
reveal.say: Flood, vandalism and hail are on the list. Deer and glass: Comprehensive. The guardrail: Collision.

reveal.text: One twist: glass broken in a collision can count as Collision, if you choose.
reveal.say: One twist: glass broken in a collision can count as Collision, if you choose.

scenes.title: Liability extras, and two exclusions
scenes.src: CA 00 01 11 20, Sec. II.A.2.a, II.B.6, II.B.8; PP 00 01 09 18, Part A; questions auto-062, auto-gap-18, auto-gap-19

draw.text: Lost earnings: up to $250 a day
Device attached to the van: not excluded

beats.text: Business Auto liability pays extras, called supplementary payments. They include bail bonds up to $2,000, and lost earnings up to $250 a day.
beats.say: Business Auto liability pays extras, called supplementary payments. They include bail bonds up to two thousand dollars, and lost earnings up to two hundred fifty dollars a day.

beats.text: Watch out: the 2018 personal auto policy's bail limit is only $250.
beats.say: Watch out: the twenty eighteen personal auto policy's bail limit is only two hundred fifty dollars.

beats.text: Two exclusions. Property Tony owns or transports, like cargo in the van, is excluded: care, custody or control.
beats.say: Two exclusions. Property Tony owns or transports, like cargo in the van, is excluded: care, custody or control.

beats.text: A loose forklift unloading the van hurts a bystander? Excluded: injury or damage from a mechanical device moving property, unless it's a hand truck or attached to the van.
beats.say: A loose forklift unloading the van hurts a bystander? Excluded: injury or damage from a mechanical device moving property, unless it's a hand truck or attached to the van.

scenes.title: Tony's van at Gus's shop
scenes.src: CA 99 37 10 01; question auto-063; memory hook mn_auto-25
scenes.plain: Covers customers' autos left in a shop's care while it services, repairs, parks or stores them.
scenes.example: Tony's van is at Gus's repair shop for brakes. If it's damaged there, Gus's garagekeepers may pay, depending on its basis.
scenes.exam: Legal liability (default): only if liable. Direct excess: regardless of liability, after the customer's insurance. Direct primary: regardless, first.

beats.text: Garagekeepers covers customers' autos left in a shop's care while it services, repairs, parks or stores them.
beats.say: Garagekeepers covers customers' autos left in a shop's care while it services, repairs, parks or stores them.

beats.text: Three bases. Legal liability, the default, pays only if the shop is legally liable. Direct excess and direct primary pay regardless of liability: excess after the customer's own insurance, primary first.
beats.say: Three bases. Legal liability, the default, pays only if the shop is legally liable. Direct excess and direct primary pay regardless of liability: excess after the customer's own insurance, primary first.

scenes.title: Gus's call: which garagekeepers basis?
scenes.src: CA 99 37 10 01, Direct Coverage Options; question auto-063; memory hook mn_auto-25

draw.text: Fault or not, nobody calls their own insurer first!

beats.text: Customer's car damaged here? My fault or not, my insurance handles it. Nobody calls their own insurer first!
beats.say: Customer's car damaged here? My fault or not, my insurance handles it. Nobody calls their own insurer first!
beats.speaker: Gus

beats.text: Gus carries garagekeepers Comprehensive. Which basis fits?
beats.say: Gus carries garagekeepers Comprehensive. Which basis fits?

options.label: Direct primary
options.win: Direct primary pays regardless of the shop's liability, and it pays first, before the customer's own insurance.

beats.text: Hail hits, and Gus's insurer pays Tony first. No blame needed.
beats.say: Hail hits, and Gus's insurer pays Tony first. No blame needed.

options.label: Legal liability, the default
options.fail: Legal liability pays only when the shop is legally liable. Gus did nothing wrong, so he isn't liable for hail.

beats.text: Hail pounds Tony's van at the shop. Gus did nothing wrong, so his policy pays nothing.
beats.say: Hail pounds Tony's van at the shop. Gus did nothing wrong, so his policy pays nothing.

options.label: Direct excess
options.fail: Direct excess pays regardless of liability, but only as excess over the customer's own insurance.

beats.text: Hail hits. Tony's own insurer pays first, and Gus's policy pays only what's left.
beats.say: Hail hits. Tony's own insurer pays first, and Gus's policy pays only what's left.

reveal.text: Three ways a shop says sorry. Legal liability: only if it was my fault.
reveal.say: Three ways a shop says sorry. Legal liability: only if it was my fault.

reveal.text: Direct excess: even if it wasn't, but your own insurer pays first. Direct primary: even if it wasn't, and I pay first.
reveal.say: Direct excess: even if it wasn't, but your own insurer pays first. Direct primary: even if it wasn't, and I pay first.

scenes.title: Auto, or mobile equipment?
scenes.src: CA 00 01 11 20, Sec. I.C.2, V.B, V.K; question auto-gap-23
scenes.plain: Off-road vehicles like bulldozers, forklifts and farm machinery; crawler-tread vehicles; vehicles used only on or next to premises you own or rent.
scenes.example: Tony's storeroom forklift is mobile equipment. A pickup with a permanently attached snowplow is still an auto.
scenes.exam: Autos: self-propelled with permanent snow-removal, road-maintenance or street-cleaning gear; cherry pickers on auto or truck chassis; FR-law vehicles.

beats.text: Tony's new storeroom forklift is mobile equipment. So are bulldozers, farm machinery, crawler-tread vehicles, and vehicles used only on or next to your premises.
beats.say: Tony's new storeroom forklift is mobile equipment. So are bulldozers, farm machinery, crawler-tread vehicles, and vehicles used only on or next to your premises.

beats.text: A pickup with a permanently attached snowplow is still an auto. So is any land vehicle subject to a compulsory or financial responsibility law.
beats.say: A pickup with a permanently attached snowplow is still an auto. So is any land vehicle subject to a compulsory or financial responsibility law.

beats.text: Without an endorsement, the Business Auto form covers mobile equipment for liability only while a covered auto carries or tows it.
beats.say: Without an endorsement, the Business Auto form covers mobile equipment for liability only while a covered auto carries or tows it.

scenes.title: Dana's endorsement toolbox
scenes.src: CA 99 10 (IRMI); CA 99 17 10 01; CA 20 01 11 20; CA 20 15 (FC&S, Rough Notes); CA 22 20, CA 22 24 (Wolters Kluwer list)

spots.label: Drive Other Car
spots.text: Tony's manager drives a company car and has no personal auto policy. This gives a named person, like him, non-owned auto coverage like a personal auto policy.

spots.label: Individual Named Insured
spots.text: For a named insured who is an individual, like Gus, a sole proprietor. It adds personal-auto-type coverage for him and his resident family members.

spots.label: Lessor additional insured
spots.text: The leasing company becomes an insured for liability, and the scheduled leased auto counts as a covered auto you own, not one you hire or borrow.

spots.label: Mobile Equipment
spots.text: A scheduled vehicle, like this scissor-lift truck, becomes a covered auto. But liability won't cover operating its machinery, like the lift falling on a worker.

spots.label: Michigan PIP and PPI
spots.text: The Business Auto form has no PIP section. In Michigan, PIP and PPI endorsements add those no-fault benefits. Symbol 5 marks owned autos subject to no-fault.

beats.text: Next, my endorsement toolbox. Tap the five glowing spots.
beats.say: Next, my endorsement toolbox. Tap the five glowing spots.

reveal.text: Drive Other Car covers a named person in autos they don't own. Individual Named Insured fits a sole proprietor and family.
reveal.say: Drive Other Car covers a named person in autos they don't own. Individual Named Insured fits a sole proprietor and family.

reveal.text: Scheduled mobile equipment becomes a covered auto, but liability won't cover operating its machinery.
reveal.say: Scheduled mobile equipment becomes a covered auto, but liability won't cover operating its machinery.

scenes.q: Tony's Pizza insures its Michigan vans under the 2020 ISO Business Auto Coverage Form. Their Michigan no-fault PIP is provided by:
choices: A Michigan Personal Injury Protection endorsement
scenes.why: The Business Auto form has no PIP section. The Michigan Personal Injury Protection endorsement adds the PIP that Michigan's no-fault law requires.

beats.text: Quick check: what gives Tony's Michigan vans their PIP?
beats.say: Quick check: what gives Tony's Michigan vans their P I P?

reveal.text: A Michigan Personal Injury Protection endorsement: the Business Auto form has no PIP section. PPI comes by endorsement too.
reveal.say: A Michigan Personal Injury Protection endorsement: the Business Auto form has no P I P section. P P I comes by endorsement too.

scenes.title: Big rigs: federal minimum limits
scenes.src: Motor Carrier Act of 1980; 49 CFR 387.9; 387.15; question auto-066

draw.text: For hire, interstate, nonhazardous, 10,001 lbs or more

beats.text: Finally, big rigs, like the semi hauling Tony's flour. The Motor Carrier Act of 1980 sets federal minimum limits.
beats.say: Finally, big rigs, like the semi hauling Tony's flour. The Motor Carrier Act of nineteen eighty sets federal minimum limits.

beats.text: For-hire interstate carriers of nonhazardous property, in vehicles of 10,001 pounds or more, need at least $750,000.
beats.say: For-hire interstate carriers of nonhazardous property, in vehicles of ten thousand one pounds or more, need at least seven hundred fifty thousand dollars.

beats.text: Oil and most hazardous materials need $1 million. Certain bulk hazardous substances, explosives and radioactive materials need $5 million.
beats.say: Oil and most hazardous materials need one million dollars. Certain bulk hazardous substances, explosives and radioactive materials need five million dollars.

beats.text: Proof of coverage: the MCS-90 endorsement.
beats.say: Proof of coverage: the M C S ninety endorsement.

items: Symbols: 1 any, 2-6 owned, 7 described, 8 hired, 9 non-owned
Symbol 7: tell the insurer about a new auto within 30 days
Specified Causes is a named list: no deer, no glass breakage
Garagekeepers: legal liability, direct excess, direct primary
Business Auto bail bonds: $2,000. Michigan PIP, PPI: by endorsement

beats.text: What a ride! Hired is 8, non-owned is 9, and direct primary pays first.
beats.say: What a ride! Hired is eight, non-owned is nine, and direct primary pays first.

beats.text: And the pizza still gets there hot.
beats.say: And the pizza still gets there hot.
